common_name: Spot On Lungwort (Silver-Speckled Pulmonaria with Salmon Pink Buds)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container starts in spring or early fall in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in part to full shade; Spot On is a Walters Gardens / Proven Winners Perennials introduction (PP33,063) with salmon-pink buds, an unusual bud color for the genus.

directions: Spot On opens flower buds in an unusual salmon-pink shade that shifts through the opening process before maturing to rich blue, giving a multi-color effect on the same stem. The silver-speckled green leaves remain tidy and attractive as a groundcover accent well after bloom finishes in late spring. Grow in organically rich, evenly moist, neutral-to-alkaline soil and avoid summer drought stress, which causes premature leaf collapse. Divide crowded clumps in early spring or immediately after flowering to maintain vigor.

common_name: Pink-a-Blue Lungwort (Two-Tone Pink Bud, Blue Flower Pulmonaria)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container starts in spring or early fall in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in part to full shade; Pink-a-Blue is a Walters Gardens / Proven Winners Perennials introduction (PP35,232), bred by Hans A. Hansen, prized for buds and open flowers that display pink and blue simultaneously on the same cluster.

directions: Pink-a-Blue produces pink buds that open to medium blue flowers, with both bud and bloom colors visible together for a two-tone display in early to mid spring. Its narrow, dark green leaves are dappled with silver spots that keep the clump attractive through the rest of the season. Site in organically rich, evenly moist soil and keep roots cool with a layer of mulch, since dry shade weakens the clump over time. Divide every few years in early spring to refresh flowering and control spread.

common_name: Rise and Shine Astilbe (Hot Pink Chinensis Hybrid with Large Plumes)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container starts in spring in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Rise and Shine is a Walters Gardens Astilbe chinensis hybrid bred for sturdier roots and brighter flower color than older chinensis varieties.

directions: Rise and Shine carries large, 8-inch pyramidal plumes of hot pink flowers on stout stems through midsummer that hold up without staking. Improved root genetics give the clump better drought and sun tolerance than many older Astilbe chinensis selections, though consistently moist soil still produces the best display. Grow in humus-rich soil in partial shade, watering through dry spells to prevent foliage from browning. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain bloom density.

common_name: Mighty Max Astilbe (Extra-Tall Purple-Flowered Chinensis Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Mighty Max is a Dutch-bred Astilbe chinensis hybrid introduced by Compass Plants B.V. in cooperation with breeder Hans van der Meer, notable for its unusually tall habit.

directions: Mighty Max stands out among Astilbe chinensis hybrids for its exceptional height, sending up thick, long plumes of regal purple-pink flowers on sturdy stems well above the toothed green foliage mound in early-to-midsummer. The large clumping habit makes a strong vertical accent at the back of a shaded border. Keep soil evenly moist and rich in organic matter, since this larger-statured selection has more foliage to support and dries out faster in sparse shade. Divide every few years in spring to keep the clump vigorous and well-shaped.

common_name: Shadow Tag Heucherella (Silver-Overlaid Foliage with Burgundy Veins, Fun and Games Series)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container starts in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Shadow Tag (USPP 37,188) belongs to Proven Winners' Fun and Games Heucherella series, a Heuchera x Tiarella hybrid bred for a mounded, container-friendly habit.

directions: Shadow Tag carries a silvery overlay across its green leaves with dark burgundy coloring that radiates outward along the veins, giving strong foliage contrast even without bloom. Sprays of bubblegum-pink flowers rise above the mound in late spring and draw bees and hummingbirds. It is semi-evergreen in milder climates and holds its mounded, non-spreading habit well in both garden beds and mixed containers. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and foliage color.

common_name: Raspberry Sundae Foamflower (Deeply Cut Foliage with Pink-Budded White Flowers)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container starts in spring or early fall in consistently moist, humus-rich woodland soil in shade; an unpatented (PPAF) Tiarella foamflower distributed through Growing Colors with deeply cut foliage and dark flower stems.

directions: Raspberry Sundae forms a tidy mound of deeply cut, heart-shaped leaves on near-black stems, with dense upright racemes opening from raspberry-pink buds into star-shaped, pale pink-and-white flowers in mid spring. The dark stems and buds give strong color contrast against the pale open blooms before they fade to white. Grow in consistently moist, organically rich soil in full to partial shade, where it slowly forms a non-aggressive clump suitable for woodland edges and shaded borders. Divide in spring every few years to rejuvenate bloom and refresh the clump.

common_name: Frost King Siberian Bugloss (Large Silver-Patterned Leaves with Dark Green Veins)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container starts in spring or early fall in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in shade; Frost King is a Darwin Perennials introduction (trade name of 'Balfroskin') that won the Garden Center Group's Retailers' Choice Award at Cultivate'25.

directions: Frost King produces oversized, heart-shaped leaves with a strong silver pattern set off by prominent dark green veins, giving a king-size scale compared to older Brunnera selections. Small sprays of bright blue, forget-me-not-like flowers appear over the emerging foliage from April into May. Grow in evenly moist, humus-rich soil in shade or morning sun with afternoon shade, since hot afternoon exposure scorches the leaves. Established clumps need little division and resent summer drought, so mulch to conserve soil moisture.

common_name: Frost Magic Siberian Bugloss (Elongated Leaves with Intense Silver Pattern)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container starts in spring or early fall in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in shade; Frost Magic is a Darwin Perennials introduction (trade name of 'Balfrosmic') with an especially heavy silver leaf pattern.

directions: Frost Magic carries an especially dense, almost solid-looking silver overlay across elongated, pointed leaves, making it one of the more heavily patterned Brunnera selections available. Bright blue flowers appear above the foliage in April and May once the plant has been through a winter chill. Grow in evenly moist, organically rich soil in shade, since the heavily silvered leaf tissue is more prone to scorch in direct sun or dry conditions than green-leaved Brunnera. Mulch to retain soil moisture and divide only occasionally, as clumps resent frequent disturbance.
